config.text:
# leasehold config for your own daemon on bench.
# Sized for 8 CPUs and 16 GiB: one slot per CPU; 2 CPUs are kept for you, and at most three quarters of the memory to any one lease.
# Made by `leasehold init` (or `leasehold setup`); `leasehold doctor` checks it. Only
# [ceiling] slots is required; the reference (docs/reference.md) lists every key.

name = "bench"
mode = "user"
ledger_dir = "ledger"            # your own daemon; `leasehold init --system` writes the machine's
# socket and ledger_dir: by default $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/leasehold/leasehold.sock and
# $XDG_STATE_HOME/leasehold; the socket is yours alone (mode 0600)

# Slots are what leases share, one per CPU given to leasehold's work; what is left is kept for
# you (your editor, browser and shell). cpus and memory are the most one lease may be given.
[ceiling]
slots = 6
cpus = 6
memory = "11g"

# Two pools. Your agents' and your own commands go in `work`; `hold --kind external` (a CI
# runner's job, a batch run) goes in `background`, which never takes work's reserved slots and
# is served after it.
[pools.work]
reserved = 3
max = 6
priority = 0

[pools.background]
reserved = 0
max = 3
priority = 1

[kinds]
work = "work"
external = "background"

[lend]
pools = []               # no lending on a personal machine; see docs/reference.md, Lending

# Containment: commands leasehold starts run in a systemd user scope weighted to their lease
# (CPUWeight 100 per slot) where your systemd user manager allows it.
[contain]
mode = "auto"            # "off": never
hard_cpu = false         # true: also cap a command at its weight in CPUs

# Memory admission: a command starts only while the memory it counts fits the budget. It
# counts what its rule or `hold --memory` declares, or, declaring none, its weight times
# assumed_per_slot ("auto": the budget over the slots, so full slots are a full budget).
[memory]
budget = "auto"          # the machine's memory less `kept`; or a size such as "12g"
kept = "25%"             # kept back for you: a share of the memory, or a size such as "4g"
assumed_per_slot = "auto"

# While memory is short, what runs keeps running and new work starts only within the memory
# measured free: none while pressure is high, then a little at a time as it eases. What waits
# says why.
[guard]
memory_pressure_on = 20.0     # PSI some avg10, percent
memory_pressure_off = 5.0
# min_available = "2g"        # default: 5% of memory, at least 512 MiB
settle_s = 30

# Which commands take a lease when an agent (or you, through the shims) runs them. The built-in
# rules cover common builds and test runs; `leasehold commands` lists them.
[commands]
heavy_weight = 4
wait_s = 300             # how long a command waits in line for its lease...
when_busy = "deny"       # ...then: "deny" it with the reason, or "run" it without a lease

# The built-in rules weigh 4 slots (builds and test runs: pytest, cargo, make, ...) and 2
# (JavaScript tooling: npm test, jest, tsc, ...), in slots and in jobs.
# On 6 slots, one of them runs at a time.
# To run two at once instead, each with fewer jobs (opt-in):
# heavy_weight = 3
# light_weight = 2
# A command that declares no memory then counts its weight times the budget over the
# slots, which may be less than it uses: declare memory for memory-heavy work (a rule's
# `memory`, or `hold --memory`).

# [[commands.rule]]
# programs = ["pytest"]
# weight = 3
# memory = "8g"          # counted against [memory]; held to this when contained (MemoryHigh)
